title: First Time in New York
novel:
Robin's [[teenage|teenage]] [[sister|sister]] Katie arrived in New York with her boyfriend to [[experience|experience]] the [[city|city]] for the first time. Robin was [[thrilled|thrill]] — until Katie [[announced|announce]] that she was planning to lose her [[virginity|virginity]] that weekend.

"Absolutely not," Robin said. "This city is not a [[love hotel|love hotel]]!"

Panicked, Robin [[enlisted|enlist]] the gang to [[sabotage|sabotage]] every [[romantic|romantic]] moment between Katie and her boyfriend. Ted was assigned to take them to the most [[unromantic|unromantic]] places in New York. Marshall was supposed to give a long, [[embarrassing|embarrass]] lecture about [[responsibility|responsible]]. Lily was tasked with [[following|follow]] them everywhere like a [[spy|spy]].

But New York had other plans. Every [[awkward|awkward]] spot Ted chose turned out to be [[magical|magic]] at night. Times Square under the rain? [[Romantic|romantic]]. A dirty subway platform with a [[saxophone|saxophone]] player? [[Romantic|romantic]]. Even the [[smelly|smell]] [[alleyway|alleyway]] behind the [[dumpster|dumpster]] became romantic when a stray cat [[purred|purr]] at them.

"This is impossible!" Robin [[groaned|groan]].

Finally, Lily got the young couple into their hotel room and locked the door — from the outside. "That should buy us some time," she said. But Robin had already [[realized|realize]] something. Katie was not a kid anymore. She was [[seventeen|seventeen]], in love, and in the most [[romantic|romantic]] city on Earth.

Robin [[knocked|knock]] on the door. "Katie? I'm sorry. Whatever you decide, I'm here for you."

The door opened. Katie hugged her sister. "Thank you," she whispered. "But I'm not ready yet."

teenage.en: relating to people aged between 13 and 19

sister.en: a girl or woman who has the same parents as you

experience.en: to do or live through something

announce.en: to tell people something officially or publicly

virginity.en: the state of never having had sex

enlist.en: to ask someone to help you with something

sabotage.en: to deliberately prevent something from succeeding

romantic.en: relating to love, or making you think about love

responsibility.en: something that is your duty to deal with

follow.en: to walk behind someone; to watch what someone does

spy.en: a person who secretly watches others to get information

magic.en: a special mysterious power that makes impossible things happen

saxophone.en: a curved musical instrument made of brass

dumpster.en: a large metal container for garbage

purr.en: (of a cat) to make a low continuous sound when happy

groan.en: to make a long low sound showing pain or disappointment

knock.en: to hit a door with your hand to ask to come in
